candidate.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
candidate.flaw_one_line: Write-protection declared with @JsonProperty(access = READ_ONLY) is not honoured on two real routes at d627a8a (unchanged in 2.20.0): (base) a getter-only read-only POJO property is merged from input when merging is enabled (setDefaultMergeable / configOverride / @JsonMerge), because the merge branch of BeanDeserializerFactory.addBeanProps has no ignorable guard; (T1) when the type has an @JsonAnySetter, addBeanProps does not register read-only names as ignorable, so read-only creator parameters (constructor, record) bind from input and read-only collections/maps are filled through their getter.

verified.exploit_entry_point: Library public API: ObjectMapper.readerForUpdating(existing).readValue(json), ObjectMapper.readValue(json, T), ObjectMapper.updateValue(existing, Map), with merging enabled mapper-wide (setDefaultMergeable(true)) or per type (configOverride(T).setMergeable(true)), or a plain mapper for the catch-all forms.
verified.scout: Probed ~45 routes with javac probes on d627a8a (work dir probe/P1.java, P2.java). Honoured on vulnerable code: plain setter/field beans, creator params (field- or param-declared) without a catch-all, records without a catch-all, builders (READ_ONLY on builder method), readerForUpdating of setter beans, unwrapped children, mix-ins, polymorphic subtypes, read-only collections without a catch-all (#1805 guard), class-level @JsonIgnoreProperties(allowGetters=true) on every route incl. catch-all and merge, renamed read-only properties. Leaking: merge on getter-only read-only POJOs (default mergeable, type override, @JsonMerge; fresh read, readerForUpdating, updateValue) and, with a catch-all, creator params (classic ctor, record, any-setter-as-creator-param), collection/map getter-as-setter, merge. Rejected: @JsonIgnore on setter + @JsonProperty getter sets the private field via INFER_PROPERTY_MUTATORS (JsonIgnore Javadoc calls this split case 'read-only (read from input into POJO)', so not clearly unintended); array shape (read-only props are dropped from positions: a functional quirk, not a write); identity PropertyGenerator with READ_ONLY id (definition error).
verified.upstream_status: No advisory or fix. BeanDeserializerFactory.addBeanProps is byte-identical in jackson-databind 2.20.0 sources. Javadoc of JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY: 'may only be read for serialization ... but not written (set) during deserialization'; nothing documents the merge or catch-all exceptions.
variants: BASE merge, mapper-wide default mergeable, readerForUpdating (the reported example): security/QuotaUpdateBypassTest.updateKeepsQuota
BASE merge, read-only declared on the field, updateValue(): security/QuotaUpdateBypassTest.fieldDeclaredQuotaKeptByUpdateValue
T1 catch-all + read-only List via getter (#1805 guard defeated): security/ExtensibleTypeBypassTest.newMemberKeepsRoles
T1 catch-all + constructor creator param (read-only declared on the field): security/ExtensibleTypeBypassTest.ticketCreatorNotFromInput
verified.project_tests_run: Hidden suite (javac + junit-platform-console, eclipse-temurin:17): vulnerable 0/8 security, 24/24 functional; reference 8/8, 24/24. Jackson's own tests: 602 tests from 106 files (every test file mentioning READ_ONLY/JsonAnySetter/JsonMerge/allowGetters/setDefaultMergeable/ConstructorProperties, plus all of deser/merge, deser/filter, deser/creators) compiled with javac and run: vulnerable 601/602, reference 601/602; the one failure (ArrayDelegatorCreatorForCollectionTest.testUnmodifiable) is a JDK17 module-opens issue present on both.

patch_checks.note: the natural fix for the example: copy the existing #1805 guard (builder.hasIgnorable) onto the merge branch. Closes the 4 base tests, misses all 4 T1 forms (ignorables are empty when there is a catch-all)
reference minus the creator marking: guards merge and getter-as-setter with the read-only names, but constructor/record parameters still bind when there is a catch-all
reference minus the getter-as-setter guard: read-only List on a catch-all type still filled
creator parameters checked for a READ_ONLY annotation on the parameter itself instead of the logical property: misses read-only declared on the field (Ticket)

the root fix the in-code comment invites ('#1805 would suggest we should block properties regardless'): register ignored names even with a catch-all, plus the precedent merge guard. Secure, but keys of @JsonIgnore'd properties stop reaching the catch-all (jackson's own AnySetterTest semantics)
treats read-only names like class-level ignorals and drops every property definition with such a name: a write-only property sharing the JSON name stops binding
refuses input aimed at ignored/read-only properties with an exception instead of ignoring it
never modifies any value through a getter (no merge-through-getter, no getter-as-setter collections)

different mechanism: with a catch-all, registers as ignorable only the ignored names that still have a property definition (read-only, not fully ignored), so BeanDeserializerBase.resolve marks creator params as usual; merge branch guarded by hasIgnorable. Read-only keys no longer reach the catch-all (not tested either way)
reference + BeanDeserializerBase.resolve also marks any creator parameter that is itself annotated READ_ONLY as ignorable

notes: source = injected, but nothing is planted: Dockerfile and checkout are identical to jackson-databind-sib2 (d627a8a). Both gaps are real, unmodified upstream code, still present in 2.20.0. No advisory or upstream fix exists. 8 security tests (all FAIL on vulnerable, all PASS on reference), 24 functional (all PASS on both). The blind pass patch and FAIRNESS.md are owed by independent agents.

traps.realistic_because: Real, unmodified jackson code, unchanged through 2.20.0. Catch-all maps for extension attributes are common on API DTOs, as are immutable constructor-built DTOs (Lombok @Value / @ConstructorProperties) and records with server-assigned fields. The existing #1805 guard and the creator ignorable marking both depend on a set that is left empty when the type has a catch-all, and the in-code comment makes that look deliberate. The example's natural fix (copy the guard 7 lines above) passes every probe of the example's type.

traps.shape: shared helper with divergent contracts (adjacent API, B-failure-modes 3a): the same ignored-names set carries read-only names (must never bind) and @JsonIgnore'd names (by design still delivered to the catch-all)
traps.realistic_because: The behaviour is jackson's own, asserted by its test suite, which ships in /app/src/test. The instruction covers it with 'input that is not aimed at a read-only property, wherever that input is delivered today'.

traps.shape: coupled visible binding (B-failure-modes 3a rank 1): a write-only input property shares the JSON name of a read-only output property
where: introspect/POJOPropertyBuilder.java:948-958 (READ_ONLY collects the explicit name into the ignored set) + introspect/POJOPropertiesCollector._renameProperties merges the write-only setter into the same logical property
traps.realistic_because: 'Id in, summary object out' under one JSON name is a common REST idiom, written with READ_ONLY/WRITE_ONLY accessors. The read-only name is in the ignored set, so a fix that treats that set as hard ignorals breaks the write-only input. The instruction states this contract explicitly.
